8 01-12-2025 Heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Ms. Priya as also the learned APP for the State, Ms.
Shashibala Verma and the learned Amicus Curiae, Ms. Aditi Sharma.

2. The present appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction and the order of sentence dated 29.10.2024 and 30.10.2024 respectively passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum-Special Judge POCSO Act, Patna in Special POCSO Case No. 7 of 2018 (arising out of Pandarak P.S. Case No. 68 of 2017) whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted under Section 376 D of the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as the 'I.P.C.') and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as the 'POCSO Act, 2012')

sentences.text: The records of this appeal have been placed before this Court to consider the prayer of the appellant for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the appeal.

4. The short facts of the case as per the written report of the mother of the victim girl i.e. PW-2 is that her daughter aged about 18 years (there appears to be manipulation) was returning back on the previous day i.e. 24.07.2017 at about 6:00 p.m. from her field after sowing seeds and on the way near Kherua Khanda, the appellant and one another had taken the daughter of the informant into the adjacent field and committed wrong with her.

On the basis of the said written report of the mother of the victim girl, Pandarak P.S. Case No. 68 of 2017 Patna High Court CR. APP (DB)
No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 was registered on 25.07.2017 under Section 376/34 of the I.P.C.
against the appellant and one another person.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that a bare perusal of the evidence of PW-3 i.e. Dr. Priyanka Kumari would show that firstly she, upon examining the victim has found her age to be approximately 18 years and secondly, in her opinion, rape has not been ascertained apart from she having not found any mark of injury anywhere on the body of the victim girl.

It is further submitted by referring to the deposition of PW-6 i.e. the Headmaster/Principal, who was at the relevant time posted as In-charge Headmaster, Primary School, Bhuapur that he, in his cross-examination has stated that no proof or birth certificate was produced in support of the date of birth of the victim at the time of admission in the school concerned and her age was mentioned orally, on the basis of which the same was entered in the school records.
Thus, it is submitted that there is no conclusive proof regarding the victim being minor as on the date of occurrence.

It is next submitted that PW-7 who is working as Director, Forensic Science Laboratory, Patna has in his evidence though proved the F.S.L report, however a bare perusal of the F.S.L. report would show that though blood stains, present on the undergarment of the victim girl, have been Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 found to be human blood, however the grouping has not been determined and instead the result of the test for blood grouping has been stated to be inconclusive.

It is thus submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the F.S.L.
report would show that neither semen was found on the undergarment of the victim girl nor there is any proof to show that the blood found thereon is that of the appellant.
Thus, it is submitted that the learned Trial Judge has, on the basis of no evidence, convicted the appellant in an unjust and illegal manner.
Lastly, it is stated that the appellant is languishing in custody since 9.8.2017, hence a sympathetic view be taken and the appellant be granted bail.

6. Per contra, the learned APP for the State Ms. Shashibala Verma and the learned Amicus Curiae appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2, Ms. Aditi Sharma have jointly opposed the prayer of the appellant for grant of bail and have submitted that the appellant has committed a heinous crime,
hence deserves no sympathy.

It is also submitted that PW-6 has produced the admission register which contains the date of birth of the victim girl who was admitted in the school in question in Class-1, thus there can be no doubt about the date of birth of the victim girl as recorded in the school records, hence the victim girl was definitely a minor as on the date of the alleged Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 occurrence

. It is next submitted that the records would bear it out that there is sufficient and reliable evidence, on the basis of which, the learned Trial Judge has convicted the appellant under Section 376 D of the I.P.C. and Section 6 of the Ranjeet Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104922380/
2 POCSO Act, 2012.
7.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having cursorily gone through the evidence on record, we prima facie find that firstly the doctor i.e. PW-3 who had examined the victim girl on 25.07.2017 itself, i.e. on the very next day of the alleged incident, has not found any mark of injury anywhere, has opined that rape is not ascertained and has found the age of the victim girl to be approximately 18 years, thus there is scant medical evidence regarding rape having been committed with the victim girl.

We further find from the evidence of PW-7, i.e. the Director, Forensic Science Laboratory, Patna, who has proved the F.S.L. report that the same is not only inconclusive but no semen was found on the undergarment of the victim girl which also creates a doubt about the occurrence in question.
Thus, we are of the prima facie opinion that there is dearth of evidence to prove the guilt of the appellant beyond all reasonable doubts.
8. We further find that the appellant has already undergone custody for more than eight years.

In this regard we Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 would gainfully refer to the Order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Saudan Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259, wherein it has been held that if an appeal is pending at the High Court stage and the convict has already undergone eight years of actual sentence, exceptions apart, in most cases bail would be the rule.

entities.text: Saudan Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has also carved out certain exceptions in cases of heinous nature of crime, however we find that the present case does not fall within the prohibited categories.
We also find that the appeal being of the year 2024, is not likely to be heard in the near future.

Therefore, considering the fact that the appellant has undergone custody of more than 8 years and the present appeal, being of the year 2024 is not likely to be heard in the near future as also for the foregoing reasons, we find that the appellant has made out a case for suspension of his sentence and grant of bail.

9. Accordingly, we direct suspension of order of sentence dated 30.10.2024 qua the appellant herein as also direct to release the appellant on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (ten thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Session Judge-VI-cum- Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1484 of 2024(8) dt.01-12-2025 Special Judge POCSO Act, Patna in Special POCSO Case No. 7 of 2018 (arising out of Pandarak P.S. Case No. 68 of 2017).
10.

It is clarified that the observation made hereinabove are prima facie and tentative in nature for the purposes of consideration of the prayer of the appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail and shall not cause any prejudice to either of the parties at the time of hearing of the main appeal.

11. List this appeal for hearing in its own turn.
(Mohit Kumar Shah, J) (Soni Shrivastava, J) GAURAV S../-
